key_insight: A fully mixed finite element formulation can stably couple Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity with reaction–diffusion calcium signaling using weak stress symmetry and mixed flux variables.
engineering_relevance: This provides a numerically robust framework for simulating mechanochemical feedback in soft tissues, with provable well-posedness and error control for solid mechanics–biochemistry coupling.
method: Model the solid with elastic stress, viscous stress, velocity, and spin as mixed unknowns.
Model calcium and inactivated IP3 with a mixed reaction–diffusion system using diffusive flux as an extra variable.
Use a commuting interpolation operator and a single inf-sup condition to obtain optimal a priori error estimates.
evidence_signal: The method is validated with numerical experiments in 2D and 3D, showing the predicted convergence rates and benchmark behavior, including mechanically driven calcium wavetrains.
watch_item: The scheme relies on weak symmetry and an inf-sup stable mixed finite element pair, so implementation quality and element choice are critical for accuracy and stability.
paper_title: Fully mixed finite element methods for the coupling of viscoelasticity and reaction-diffusion models
